quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If the fog is too thick to see through, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What does excessive speed cause?

options.text: It does not increase crash risk.
It improves your ability to react to danger.
It often leads to risky driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often leads to risky driving decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. Going too fast does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving choices.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right for road construction.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about hazards ahead. This sign tells you to slow down for a sharp turn.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no traffic from either direction can cross to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules are a guide, but no driver should assume they have the right-of-way. Always watch the situation. Give up your legal right-of-way if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A construction worker with a flag is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction worker with a flag is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a flagger ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear orange, yellow, or bright jackets and use paddles and flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: A railroad crossing.
A pedestrian crossing.
A no passing zone.

questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn about hazards. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Expect unexpected conditions.
Expect construction workers to get out of your way.

questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected hazards. Drive with extra care for your safety, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: How should you press the gas pedal?

options.text: Slowly and smoothly
As fast as possible
With light taps

questions.explanation: Press the gas pedal slowly and smoothly. Pressing too quickly can make the wheels spin or cause the car to slide, especially on wet roads.

questions.question: What do you do at a flashing yellow traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely at the intersection.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed with caution. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: What do you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When can you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on water instead of the road. What should you do to prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed steady.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slowing down prevents hydroplaning.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles required to stop at crossings and watch for trains coming from both directions.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is about to end.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. You must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if there are no oncoming vehicles
Wherever signs and pavement markings allow passing
In a curve if there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and pavement markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass at intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleyways. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead. Only pass where signs and pavement markings permit it, and only if you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.explanation: A person's weight, biological sex, food in their stomach, and how much they have drunk all affect alcohol absorption. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual events causes traffic congestion. Avoid doing this.

questions.question: If you need to use your lights while driving due to weather or light conditions, what should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with or without a curb, or uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. Your car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: This symbol is used for:

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle shows it moves slowly. You may see it on farm equipment, roadwork vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks like a solid orange triangle during the day and a hollow red triangle at night.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Eating, drinking coffee, or showering will not speed this up.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for them to cross the street.
Turn right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they have crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to drive on if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving, including drugs for colds, allergies, or anxiety. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.
